If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecasted price by 1–2% in the early horizon (days 1–7) to avoid over-optimism.

If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecasted price by 1–2% in the early horizon (days 1–7) to compensate for bearish bias.

If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon (days 8–15), reduce forecasted price by 1–3% in the mid-horizon to reflect sentiment reversal.

If sentiment is mixed (alternating 0.33–0.67) in the last 3 days, apply a 0.5–1.5% downward adjustment in the late horizon (days 16–30) to dampen volatility.

If sentiment is uniformly positive over 5+ days, increase forecasted price by 0.5–1.5% in the late horizon (days 16–30) to capture sustained bullish momentum.

If sentiment is uniformly negative over 5+ days, reduce forecasted price by 0.5–1.5% in the late horizon (days 16–30) to reflect entrenched bearish sentiment.
